name: Saṅkalpa
सङ्कल्प
Intention
baby: Pregnancy is counted from your last period, so conception happens around the end of week 2. By week 4 a tiny ball of cells has nestled into the womb and is forming the layers that will become every organ.
note: Most people don’t know they are pregnant yet. Whenever you begin this book is the right time.
mind: Make a calm playlist for the months ahead.
body: Learn belly breathing — your anchor for all 40 weeks.
heart: What did you feel when you first found out?
partner: Book the first antenatal appointment together.
calm: Hand on belly. Whisper: ‘Welcome.’

name: Bīja
बीज
The seed
baby: The neural tube — the beginning of the brain and spinal cord — is forming and will close by the end of week 6. The first heart cells are gathering.
note: This is why folic acid matters so much now: it greatly lowers the risk of neural-tube problems.
mind: Asato mā — ‘lead me from darkness to light’ (page 20).
body: Three slow breaths whenever nausea rises.
heart: What worry is on your mind? What wish is hiding inside it?
partner: Take over one daily chore so she can rest.
calm: Breathe in ‘I am’, breathe out ‘here’.

name: Hṛdaya
हृदय
Heart
baby: A tiny heart begins to beat around now and may be seen on an early scan. The neural tube is closing.
note: Suśruta wrote that the heart ‘becomes manifest’ in the 4th month; science now sees the first beats far earlier.
mind: Three soft Oṃs, morning and night.
body: Release your neck and shoulders after screen time.
heart: Three good things from this week:
partner: Keep water and a dry snack within her reach, always.
calm: Feel your own heartbeat for one minute.

name: Prāṇa
प्राण
Breath of life
baby: Arm and leg buds are lengthening and the brain is growing quickly. Your baby is now about the size of a jamun.
note: Tiredness and nausea are common now. Rest is real work for two.
mind: Tell baby one thing you love about your home.
body: Five rounds of gentle humming before sleep.
heart: What kind of parent do you hope to be?
partner: Read the warning signs on page 8 together.
calm: Long, slow out-breath — three times.

name: Sparśa
स्पर्श
Touch
baby: Fingers are beginning to form. Around now the skin around the mouth starts to respond to touch — the first of the senses to wake.
note: Touch is the earliest sense to develop; hearing and sight follow much later.
mind: Read this week’s wisdom line slowly, twice.
body: Begin pelvic-floor squeezes — 3 times a day.
heart: Who can you share both joy and worry with this week?
partner: Ask: what smell or food is bothering you? Then remove it.
calm: Rest your hands together and feel their warmth.

name: Śānti
शान्ति
Peace
baby: All the main organs have begun to form. Baby makes tiny movements — far too small for you to feel yet.
note: Feeling up and down is normal. If low mood lasts most days for two weeks, tell your doctor.
mind: Saha nāvavatu — ‘may we two be protected together’ (page 20).
heart: What would you like to tell baby today?
spirit: Try the simple kolam on page 18.
partner: Plan a slow evening walk together.
calm: Say ‘śānti’ silently on each out-breath.

name: Mūla
मूल
Root
baby: Baby is now called a fetus. The vital organs are in place and will spend the coming months growing and maturing.
note: First-trimester tiredness is caused by real changes in your body. Resting is productive.
mind: Ten minutes of music with your feet up.
body: A 10–20 minute walk on most days.
heart: What would you like to tell your baby about your family’s roots?
spirit: Root (Mūlādhāra) check-in: what makes you feel safe?
partner: Take charge of dinner twice this week.
calm: Feel your feet on the floor. You are held.

name: Svāda
स्वाद
Taste
baby: Taste buds are forming, and baby has begun swallowing small amounts of amniotic fluid.
note: Flavours from your food later reach the amniotic fluid — a first ‘taste’ of home.
mind: Describe your favourite meal to baby.
heart: How has support felt this week? What would help more?
spirit: Kind wishes for yourself and baby.
partner: Make her comfort meal — the pregnancy-safe version.
calm: Taste one sip of water slowly.

name: Jala
जल
Water
baby: Baby can open and close the fingers and curl the toes. The first-trimester screening scan often happens around 11–14 weeks.
note: Write your questions for the scan on page 77 so you don’t forget them.
mind: A sound bath of water sounds — rain, river, waves.
body: Gentle cat–cow to ease the back.
heart: What are you hoping to hear at the scan?
spirit: One calm minute before the scan.
partner: Come to the scan, and ask your own questions too.
calm: Imagine a still pond. Breathe.

name: Pallava
पल्लव
New leaf
baby: The first trimester ends this week. Fingerprints are beginning to form and the vocal cords are developing.
note: The risk of miscarriage falls considerably after the first trimester.
mind: Read this week’s wisdom line; keep it on a card.
body: Stretch your neck and shoulders, slowly.
heart: A letter to close the first trimester:
partner: Celebrate the end of the first trimester with something she enjoys.
calm: Thank your body for these 13 weeks.

name: Utsāha
उत्साह
Renewed energy
baby: Baby moves arms and legs, and can squint and make faces. Many mothers feel more energy now.
note: Use the energy for gentle activity — and keep resting when you need to.
heart: Three good things from this week:
partner: Plan a gentle outing together.
calm: Smile, and feel the smile in your belly.

name: Puṣṭi
पुष्टि
Nourishment
baby: Bones are hardening and the ears are moving into their final position.
note: From around 19 weeks baby begins to respond to sound — start choosing your songs.
mind: Choose a lullaby in your mother tongue (pages 22–23).
heart: Picture baby’s face. What do you imagine?
spirit: Draw a kolam with three loops.
partner: Find out about antenatal classes near you.
calm: Breathe in nourishment, breathe out thanks.

name: Spanda
स्पन्द
Flutter
baby: You may soon feel the first flutters — usually between 16 and 24 weeks, often later in a first pregnancy.
note: Not feeling movement yet at 16 weeks is normal. Patterns become clearer after 24 weeks.
mind: Sing your chosen lullaby every evening.
heart: Hands on belly: what do you feel?
partner: Rest a hand on the bump each evening — flutters come soon.
calm: Notice the smallest sensation in your body.

name: Smṛti
स्मृति
Memory
baby: Fat begins to form under the skin and the umbilical cord grows stronger.
note: Making memories now — photos, recordings, letters — becomes a gift for your child later.
mind: Say hello to baby three times today.
body: Wall pelvic tilts for the lower back.
heart: Record your first voice message. What did you say?
spirit: Sacral (Svādhiṣṭhāna) check-in: what brings you joy?
partner: Record a voice message for baby (page 73).
calm: Remember a happy childhood moment.

name: Gīta
गीत
Song
baby: The structures of the inner ear are developing fast. Very soon baby will begin to respond to sound.
note: Low sounds — like voices and humming — pass through the womb most easily.
mind: Choose ONE family song to sing all pregnancy.
heart: How did baby’s other parent feel talking to the bump?
spirit: Listen to silence for one minute.
partner: Choose the family lullaby together.
calm: Hum one note until the breath is gently done.

name: Śruti
श्रुति
Hearing
baby: In research, the first responses to sound appear at around 19 weeks — starting with low tones.
note: Science-backed: babies hear in the womb and come to know familiar voices. It does not make a baby ‘smarter’ — it builds familiarity.
mind: Talk to baby every day from today.
body: Alternate-nostril breathing — never hold the breath.
heart: What did you tell baby today?
spirit: Soft gaze at the Śrī Yantra (page 17).
partner: Talk to the bump for 5 minutes each evening.
calm: Listen to your own breath.

name: Madhya
मध्य
Halfway
baby: Halfway! A protective coating (vernix) covers the skin. The detailed anomaly scan usually happens at 18–22 weeks. (From now, length is measured head to heel.)
note: Every pregnancy grows at its own pace; sizes here are averages.
body: A walk where you can still talk comfortably.
heart: A letter at the halfway point:
partner: Go with her to the anomaly scan.
calm: Halfway. Breathe in what has been; breathe out what will be.

name: Gati
गति
Movement
baby: Movements grow stronger. You may notice times of day when baby is more active.
note: Start noticing your baby’s own pattern — there is no ‘right’ number of kicks.
mind: Tell baby what you are doing as you do it.
body: Gentle warrior II with a chair nearby.
heart: Three good things from this week:
partner: Feel for kicks with your hand on the bump.
calm: Wait for a kick. Breathe until it comes.

name: Rūpa
रूप
Form
baby: Lips, eyelids and eyebrows are more distinct. Baby’s grip is getting stronger.
note: Looks are shaped by genes, not by what you see or do — let go of any such worry.
mind: Ask an elder to teach you a lullaby.
heart: Imagine holding baby’s hand. What do you feel?
partner: Start the family tree with the elders (page 74).
calm: Open and close your hands slowly.

name: Dhvani
ध्वनि
Sound
baby: Hearing is maturing; loud sudden sounds may make baby startle or move.
note: Keep music at a comfortable volume — never place headphones on the belly.
mind: Music with your feet up, 20 minutes.
heart: Which sounds do you want baby to know?
partner: Make a ‘calm sounds’ playlist with her (page 72).
calm: Name 3 sounds you can hear right now.

name: Jīvana
जीवन
Life
baby: The lungs are forming branches. The glucose (sugar) test is often done between 24 and 28 weeks.
note: From now on, report any reduction in baby’s movements straight away.
spirit: Kind wishes for everyone in your family.
partner: Go with her for the sugar (GTT) test; bring a snack for afterwards.
calm: Breathe in ‘life’, breathe out ‘love’.

name: Kamala
कमल
Lotus
baby: The hands are fully formed and baby responds to both touch and sound. Hair is growing.
note: In a small study, babies moved more when their mothers stroked their belly.
body: Tree pose — always beside a wall.
heart: What did baby do when you touched your belly?
partner: Give a gentle hand or foot massage.
calm: Picture a lotus rising clean from muddy water.

name: Netra
नेत्र
Eyes
baby: Around 26–28 weeks the eyes begin to open and blink. Baby may react to bright light through your belly.
note: Sight is the last sense to mature — most of it develops after birth.
heart: Three good things from this week:
spirit: Soft gaze at the yantra (or a flower).
partner: Massage her feet this week (BODY box).
calm: Close your eyes; see soft golden light.

name: Sandhi
सन्धि
Threshold
baby: The second trimester ends. Baby has regular sleep–wake cycles and a very active brain.
note: The third trimester begins next week — side sleeping and movement awareness become important.
body: Open seated twist on a chair.
heart: A letter to close the second trimester:
spirit: Draw a kolam for the threshold of your home.
partner: Start planning the godh bharai / sīmantham (page 75).
calm: Stand in a doorway. Breathe. Step through.

name: Smaraṇa
स्मरण
Remembering
baby: Baby can open the eyes and respond to light. This week begins the third trimester.
note: Science-backed: from now on, go to sleep on your side — it lowers the risk of stillbirth.
mind: Begin ‘same story, same song’ — every evening until birth.
body: Practise falling asleep on your side.
heart: What help would make the next 12 weeks easier?
partner: Set up pillows for side sleeping.
calm: Turn to your side. Breathe. Rest.

name: Mṛdu
मृदु
Gentleness
baby: Muscles and lungs are maturing. Kicks and stretches are strong and easy to feel.
note: Know your baby’s pattern. If movements slow down or change, call your hospital at once — don’t wait.
body: Wall pelvic tilts for back ease.
heart: Imagine the first time baby hears your voice outside the womb.
partner: Learn the movement rule: if baby moves less, call the hospital now.
calm: Be gentle with yourself today.

name: Prakāśa
प्रकाश
Light
baby: The brain’s surface is folding into ridges as it grows quickly.
note: Your nourishing food, sleep and calm all support this growth — there are no shortcuts or guarantees.
heart: What does baby’s other parent sing or say?
partner: Prepare the documents folder for the hospital bag (page 78).
calm: Picture morning light filling the room.

name: Prema
प्रेम
Love
baby: All five senses are working. Baby turns the head and may hiccup — you may feel little rhythmic jumps.
note: Hiccups are normal and harmless.
heart: What is love teaching you right now?
partner: Write your own letter to baby.
calm: Hand on heart, hand on belly.

name: Dhairya
धैर्य
Courage
baby: Baby practises breathing movements and has toenails. Many babies settle head-down around now.
note: Breathing practice now is for you — slow breaths are a skill that helps in labour.
partner: Visit the hospital: find parking and the labour ward.
calm: Breathe in courage, breathe out fear.

name: Sneha
स्नेह
Affection
baby: Bones are hardening (the skull stays soft for birth). Antibodies pass to baby from you.
note: Your antibodies give baby some early protection after birth.
heart: Write one blessing from an elder:
spirit: Heart (Anāhata) check-in: who do you feel close to?
partner: Arrange support for the first weeks at home.
calm: Think of someone who loves you.

name: Āśīrvāda
आशीर्वाद
Blessing
baby: The lungs are maturing and fat is giving baby a rounder look. Many families hold the godh bharai / sīmantham around now.
note: Celebrations are about joy and support — no sex-prediction games or rituals.
spirit: Draw a rangoli or kolam for the celebration.
partner: Host the celebration so she only has to rest and enjoy.
calm: Receive. You don’t have to do anything.

name: Viśrānti
विश्रान्ति
Rest
baby: The kidneys are fully developed. Most growth now is weight gain.
note: Sleep may be harder now — rest whenever you can, on your side.
heart: Three good things from this week:
partner: Plan safe transport to hospital (and a car seat if you drive).
calm: Let the bed hold all your weight.

name: Prastuti
प्रस्तुति
Readiness
baby: Baby is getting ready. The head may ‘engage’ (drop) into the pelvis, making breathing a little easier.
note: Pack the hospital bag this week (page 78).
heart: Record your lullaby for baby. Which song?
spirit: Apāna mudrā — traditionally kept for these last weeks.
partner: Practise the route to hospital — at night too.
calm: Everything you need is already within you.

name: Pūrṇatā
पूर्णता
Fullness
baby: Early term. Baby practises sucking and grasping and is ready for the outside world.
note: Learn the newborn danger signs on page 80.
body: Practise the long out-breath for labour.
partner: Learn the newborn danger signs on page 80.
calm: Breathe out longer than you breathe in.

name: Dhyāna
ध्यान
Stillness
baby: The fine body hair (lanugo) is shedding. Baby is ready to meet you.
note: Waiting is part of the journey. Most babies are born between 37 and 42 weeks.
spirit: Sit in stillness for one minute.
partner: Cook and freeze two simple meals for after the birth.
calm: Be still. Baby is near.

name: Udaya
उदय
Dawn
baby: Baby is fully ready. The brain is still growing fast — and will keep growing for years after birth.
note: Keep watching baby’s movements right up to birth; they should not slow down.
heart: Who will you call first when baby arrives?
spirit: Look at the moon — a new phase is coming.
partner: Keep your phone charged and stay reachable.
calm: Imagine the first light of dawn.

name: Janma
जन्म
Birth
baby: Your due date. Only a few babies arrive exactly on the day — anywhere from 37 to 42 weeks is normal.
note: If your pregnancy goes past the due date, your doctor will advise you on monitoring and next steps.
mind: Your story and song — one more time before you meet.
heart: Your final letter before you meet:
spirit: Kind wishes for the birth and all who help.
partner: Hold her hand. You are both ready.
calm: Welcome, little one.
